analysis:
This PR changes only docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md. The visible patch (head lines 676-684, outside the two supplied head excerpts) rewords when a start wait in the pair setup ends after a stop: a stop during model download or copy, during load, and at the test request counts; the leading Mac's status carries a stop count; a bare "Stopped" status is no longer treated as a stop after 20 seconds. I reviewed the supplied excerpts at lines 864-1751 and found them unchanged context. They describe cluster local-only serving, the key/relay design, the free-disk gate, qualification records, prefix cache scoping, update drain, and the GPU limit command.

No code, auth, crypto, key-handling or wire-contract behavior changes here. The prose is consistent with the retained controls. It says Only me never contacts a coordinator, and the local API has no TLS and requires a key. Tenant-scoped SSD prefix cache (T-041), a manifest-pinned model copy over the keyed link, and gpu-limit run as root behind confirmation plus an administrator prompt (TB-014/T-062) all match the model. Cache-scope wording (no cache scope means nothing kept) is consistent with the T-041 mitigation.

Remaining unverified: the actual stop-count/status implementation (the cluster service and status protocol) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm it authenticates stop requests or that the joining Mac cannot be tricked into reporting a spurious stop. The docs-only change gives no basis for a finding. A possible integration question is whether a same-network peer can forge the stop count (a DoS-class concern), but it is unverified, and the cable link is described as keyed and authenticated.
